newsitem.title: USA: Dresdner combines U.S. securities units.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner combines U.S. securities units.

text.p: Dresdner Bank AG said Wednesday it has started operating its new investment banking subsidiary Dresdner Kleinwort Benson North America LLC, which combines Dresdner Securities (USA) Inc with Kleinwort Benson North America Inc.
Dresdner Bank AG acquired Kleinwort Benson Group Plc in August of 1995 for $1.5 billion. Dresdner said the Federal Reserve Board approved the merger of the U.S. securities units on July 15, 1996.

Dresdner said the unit will have full Section 20 powers under the U.S. Glass-Steagall law. Section 20 provides for securities affiliates of commercial banks to engage in corporate debt and securities dealing subject to certain limitations.
Dresdner Kleinwort Benson North America is a member of the National Association of Securities Dealers, and will apply to become a member of the New York Stock Exchange, Dresdner said.
"Our clients will benefit from Dresdner's global reach, long-standing relationships and triple-A credit rating," George Fugelsang, chief executive of Dresdner North America said in a statement.

He continued, "These strengths will be complemented by Kleinwort's sector-focused corporate advisory skills and recognized equity underwriting and global research capabilities, which we hope to extend further in North America."
